b: Aadhi is a queer writer and poet whose works explore themes of identity, caste, and contemporary issues. The first poetry collection, Pennappan , earned the Kerala Sahitya Akademi Youth Poetry Award, the K. V.…
f: Aadhi is a queer writer and poet whose works explore themes of identity, caste, and contemporary issues. The first poetry collection, Pennappan , earned the Kerala Sahitya Akademi Youth Poetry Award, the K. V. Sudhakaran Memorial Literary Award, and A. Ayyappan Memorial Poetry Award. A poem from this collection, translated into English by poet K. Satchidanandan, was published in the Indian Literature journal by the Sahitya Akademi. Aadhi’s poems have also been included in the syllabi of Calicut University and Mahatma Gandhi University. Currently, Aadhi is pursuing research on “The Variations in Kerala Modernity” under the guidance of Sunil P. Elayidom at the Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit. Aadhi holds a bachelor’s degree in Malayalam Language and Literature from the Government Arts and Science College, Koduvally, a postgraduate degree with distinction from the Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit, and a B.Ed. from the Government College of Teacher Education, Kozhikode. In addition to poetry, Aadhi writes insightful articles on queerness, caste, and Hindutva, contributing to critical discourse on these significant topics.

b: Adv. K. S. Sabarinadhan is the United Democratic Front (UDF) Parliamentary Party Leader in the Thiruvananthapuram Corporation. He previously served two terms as a member of the Kerala Legislative Assembly, from 2015-21.…
f: Adv. K. S. Sabarinadhan is the United Democratic Front (UDF) Parliamentary Party Leader in the Thiruvananthapuram Corporation. He previously served two terms as a member of the Kerala Legislative Assembly, from 2015-21. He is also the General Secretary of the Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC). Before entering active politics, he worked in the corporate sector and later in the development sector at the Chairman’s Office of Tata Trusts. He played a key role in implementing projects across various Indian states in the fields of healthcare, nutrition and livelihoods. He has also written and spoken on a range of subjects, including Kerala politics, economics, and various social issues. He holds an MBA from the Management Development Institute, Gurugram, a degree in Electrical Engineering from the College of Engineering, Thiruvananthapuram, and an LLB from the University of Kerala.

b: Ajit Isaac is the founder and chairman of Quess Corp, India’s leading business service provider and a global leader in workforce management solutions employing over 600,000 people across 9 countries. Isaac founded Quess…
f: Ajit Isaac is the founder and chairman of Quess Corp, India’s leading business service provider and a global leader in workforce management solutions employing over 600,000 people across 9 countries. Isaac founded Quess Corp in 2007, building on nearly 15 years of experience in corporate roles within the human resources industry and his success in founding Peopleone Consulting, which was subsequently acquired by Adecco. He is credited with being one of the pioneers of temporary staffing in India. Isaac’s contribution has been widely recognised – he was named Global Workforce Icon at the News9 Global Summit 2024 in Stuttgart, Germany, was nominated for the Forbes India Leadership Award, and was a finalist for the E&Y Entrepreneur of the Year award. Besides being a successful entrepreneur, Isaac is a philanthropist at heart who strongly believes in the idea of giving back to society. His commitment to contribute to the welfare of people led to the creation of the Care Works Foundation, which focuses on providing education to underprivileged children and now serves as the CSR arm of Quess (Quess Foundation). In addition, he supports various causes through the Ajit Isaac Foundation, a personal philanthropic organisation dedicated to initiatives in healthcare, livelihoods, and creating opportunities. Isaac holds a master’s degree from Madras University and is a British Chevening Scholar from the University of Leeds, UK. He is a distinguished founding trustee of Ashoka University and also serves on the Board of Governors at St. Joseph’s University in Bengaluru.

b: Chinmayi Sripada is an Indian singer, voice actor, entrepreneur and former radio and television presenter. She has worked extensively across Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi and Hindi cinema, with a career…
f: Chinmayi Sripada is an Indian singer, voice actor, entrepreneur and former radio and television presenter. She has worked extensively across Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi and Hindi cinema, with a career spanning playback singing, dubbing, composition and live performance. She rose to prominence with her acclaimed rendition of “Oru Deivam Thantha Poovae”, composed by A. R. Rahman for Mani Ratnam’s Kannathil Muthamittal (2002). She made her voice-acting debut with Sillunu Oru Kaadhal (2006) and received the Nandi Award for Best Female Dubbing Artist in 2010. As a composer, she released “Laali”, a short lullaby created as part of Instagram’s #1MinMusic initiative. Her works have earned her several honours, including the Tamil Nadu State Film Award for Best Female Playback Singer, as well as the Filmfare and SIIMA Awards across multiple languages. Beyond music and cinema, Chinmayi is an entrepreneur and the founder and CEO of ‘Blue Elephant’, a translation services company. She has also ventured into the beauty and wellness sector through ‘SkinRoute’ and ‘Deep Skin Dialogues’. Chinmayi is also recognised for her advocacy for women’s rights and as one of the prominent voices of India’s #MeToo movement. In 2018, she publicly spoke about sexual harassment in the Tamil film and television industry. She has since continued to speak about workplace harassment, gender discrimination and the need for greater accountability, advocating for safer and more equitable working environments for women in the industry.

b: Dhanya Rajendran is the co-founder and Editor-in-Chief of The News Minute, a digital newsroom that reports on politics, culture, and society across south India. Dhanya has received the Chameli Devi Jain Award for…
f: Dhanya Rajendran is the co-founder and Editor-in-Chief of The News Minute, a digital newsroom that reports on politics, culture, and society across south India. Dhanya has received the Chameli Devi Jain Award for Outstanding Woman Journalist and the Red Ink ‘Journalist of the Year’ Award from the Mumbai Press Club. She was also nominated for the RSF (Reporters Without Borders) Global Impact Award in 2025 for her work defending press freedom. She heads Digipub, India’s largest digital media organisation with around 120 members and is an executive board member of the International Press Institute of Vienna.

b: Dinu Veyil is a young human rights defender, research scholar and orator. He is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Sociology at the Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit, Kalady. He is the founder of…
f: Dinu Veyil is a young human rights defender, research scholar and orator. He is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Sociology at the Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit, Kalady. He is the founder of ‘Dhisha’, a non-profit organisation that has been working to defend the rights of marginalised communities for the past ten years. Dinu has received the Dr. B. R. Ambedkar National Meritorious Award from the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India; the Karma Award in 2015 from the MKR Foundation; the K. V. Anoop Memorial Award in 2017; the Saahas Youth Award in 2020 from WISCOMP, a South Asian organisation functioning under the Dalai Lama’s Foundation for Universal Responsibility, for his interventions in ensuring gender justice on campuses across the state; and the Ambedkar Caravan Saradhi Award, instituted by the All India SC/ST Railway Employees Association, Palakkad Division.

b: Dr. Amita V. Joseph comes with four decades of experience spanning the corporate, legal and development sectors. She has a degree in Law (Delhi University), postgraduate qualifications in Human Rights Law (ILI, Delhi)…
f: Dr. Amita V. Joseph comes with four decades of experience spanning the corporate, legal and development sectors. She has a degree in Law (Delhi University), postgraduate qualifications in Human Rights Law (ILI, Delhi) and Management (AIM), and a PhD from Deakin University, Australia. Amita supports public causes, public interest work, and the work of many nonprofits on whose boards she serves pro bono, including the Business & Community Foundation (BCF), the Academy of Fine Arts & Literature, and Consumer Voice, amongst others. She is an independent member of POSH Committees, the Ethics and National Grievance Redressal Committee (GRC) of the CRWI, etc. A number of her articles and case studies have been published in magazines and journals, and she has taught courses at IIFT, IICA, etc. Amita has served on many juries and initiated the NDTV CSR Award and the ‘Corporate Responsibility Watch’ (CRW) with Praxis and other organisations on aligning Business Responsibility (BRR) and CSR. She has been a volunteer in the cause of support to homeless citizens since 1999. She was awarded the Deakin VC Award for significant alumni contribution in 2019 and the NS Books Award for outstanding community service in 2011.

b: Dr. John Brittas is a Rajya Sabha MP from Kerala, representing the Communist Party of India (Marxist), and serves as the Leader of the CPI(M) Parliamentary Group in the Rajya Sabha. Known for his articulate…
f: Dr. John Brittas is a Rajya Sabha MP from Kerala, representing the Communist Party of India (Marxist), and serves as the Leader of the CPI(M) Parliamentary Group in the Rajya Sabha. Known for his articulate interventions and proactive engagement with matters of national importance, he has consistently championed democratic values, social justice, linguistic diversity, federal principles and electoral transparency. In October 2026, Dr. Brittas joined protests in New Delhi demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged electoral-roll irregularities, and was among those detained during the subsequent police action. His parliamentary contributions have earned him several distinctions, including the Lokmat Best Parliamentarian Award and the Sansad Ratna Puraskaar, and he serves on important parliamentary committees, including the Committee on Public Undertakings and the Standing Committee on External Affairs. Before entering Parliament, he built a career spanning over three decades in journalism and senior media management, reporting on several defining moments in India’s political and international landscape. His coverage from Delhi, Pakistan and Nepal received national attention, and he was the first Indian journalist to report from Baghdad during the US-Iraq conflict. His widely acclaimed “Baghdad Diary” remains a notable account of his reporting from the conflict zone. He has accompanied Indian Prime Ministers on official visits to several countries, including the United States, Russia, Germany, and Switzerland, and served as an Advisor to the Chief Minister of Kerala from 2016 to 2021. A familiar and respected voice in national public discourse and television journalism, he continues to contribute to the media and broadcasting sector

b: Dr. Stanly Johny is a journalist specialising in geopolitics, the Middle East, and Indian foreign policy. He is the International Affairs Editor at The Hindu and visiting faculty at the Department of International…
f: Dr. Stanly Johny is a journalist specialising in geopolitics, the Middle East, and Indian foreign policy. He is the International Affairs Editor at The Hindu and visiting faculty at the Department of International Studies at Krea University, Andhra Pradesh, and the Asian College of Journalism, Chennai. He holds a PhD in International Affairs from Jawaharlal Nehru University and is an International Visitor Leadership Program (IVLP) Fellow of the United States (US) Department of State. He is also an alumnus of the India-Australia Youth Dialogue and the Commonwealth’s Indo-Pacific Thinkers’ Programme. Johny has reported from multiple international locations including Brussels, Moscow, Amman, Ramallah, and Tel Aviv. His work has appeared in Economic and Political Weekly , The Hindu Business Line , Frontline , and Business Standard , and he has contributed to the Middle East Institute, the Lee Kuan Yew School of Public Policy, and the Manohar Parrikar Institute for Defence Studies and Analyses. He is the author of The ISIS Caliphate: From Syria to the Doorsteps of India (2018), The Comrades and the Mullahs: India, Afghanistan and the New Asian Geopolitics (2022), and Original Sin: Israel, Palestine and the Revenge of Old West Asia (2024). He has also edited Despatches: Reports from Around the World and The Hindu Profiles , both published by The Hindu Group, and contributed chapters to edited volumes on foreign policy and global politics, including India’s National Security Annual Review 2016–17, published by Routledge.

b: Dr. Vijoo Krishnan is a peasant leader and political activist deeply involved in agrarian issues. He is the General Secretary of the All India Kisan Sabha (AIKS) and a member of the Politburo of the Communist Party of…
f: Dr. Vijoo Krishnan is a peasant leader and political activist deeply involved in agrarian issues. He is the General Secretary of the All India Kisan Sabha (AIKS) and a member of the Politburo of the Communist Party of India (Marxist). He holds an MPhil and PhD from Jawaharlal Nehru University, with a specialisation in the Indian agrarian economy. Before becoming a full-time political activist, he headed the Department of Political Science at St. Joseph’s College, Bengaluru. Krishnan has worked closely with farmers’ and land-rights movements since the late 2000s, and is one of the key organisers of the ‘Bhoomi Adhikar Andolan’, a coalition working on land and livelihood rights. He played a central role in organising the Kisan Long March from Nashik to Mumbai in 2018, as well as farmers’ mobilisations in Rajasthan, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Delhi. He has also been involved in campaigns on farmers’ debt and suicides, minimum support prices, forest rights, and the rights of tenant farmers. As a leader of the All India Kisan Sabha, he was closely involved in the 2020–21 farmers’ agitation against the three farm laws. He has written about the movement, and more broadly about agrarian issues and rural livelihoods, in publications including The Hindu and Frontline. He was the President of the Jawaharlal Nehru University Students’ Union in 1998–99, and has been involved in student, labour, and peasant movements for several decades. He is also a photographer whose work documents the everyday lives of working-class communities.

b: Zakir Thomas, a seasoned Indian Revenue Service officer, has held several high-profile roles throughout his extensive career, including Director General (Systems) and Chief Commissioner of Income Tax. He has served as…
f: Zakir Thomas, a seasoned Indian Revenue Service officer, has held several high-profile roles throughout his extensive career, including Director General (Systems) and Chief Commissioner of Income Tax. He has served as Principal Director (Investigation) for Kerala and Lakshadweep, and as Principal Commissioner of Income Tax in Bangalore. At the Central Board of Direct Taxes, he contributed to policy formulation, particularly in intellectual property, e-governance, and innovation. He was honored with the prestigious Finance Minister’s Award during his time as Additional Director General of the Directorate of Income Tax (Risk Assessment). With over 30 years of experience across key ministries like Finance, Science and Technology, and Human Resource Development, Zakir Thomas also founded and led the Open Source Drug Discovery (OSDD) program at CSIR, focusing on innovative approaches to drug discovery. His contributions include serving as the head of the Director General’s Technical Cell at CSIR and as the Registrar of Copyrights. He currently serves as the DPIIT IPR Chair Professor at the National Law School of India University (NLSIU), Bengaluru.

b: E. Santhosh Kumar is a Malayalam writer well known for his novels, short stories, essays, travel writing, translations, and children’s literature. Born in Pattikkad, Thrissur, in 1969, he studied at Sree Kerala Varma…
f: E. Santhosh Kumar is a Malayalam writer well known for his novels, short stories, essays, travel writing, translations, and children’s literature. Born in Pattikkad, Thrissur, in 1969, he studied at Sree Kerala Varma College and St. Thomas College, Thrissur. He worked with the National Insurance Company for more than three decades before taking voluntary retirement in 2020 to devote more time to writing. He has, so far, published over 25 books across various genres. His works include the short story collections Chavukali , Narakangalude Upama , and Moonnu Viralukal , and the novels Andhakaranazhi , Njaanabharam , and Tapomayiyude Achan . His first published story, Galapagos , later appeared as part of a collection. Chavukali received the Kerala Sahitya Akademi Award for Story in 2006, while Andhakaranazhi received the award for Novel in 2012. The English translation of Andhakaranazhi , titled Island of Lost Shadows , was shortlisted for the Crossword Translation Award in 2016. His works have been translated into multiple Indian and international languages including English, Hindi, Tamil, Kannada, Gujarati, German, Bengali, and Arabic. Kumar has received several literary awards, including the Kerala Children’s Literature Institute Award and the Nooranad Haneef Memorial Novel Award. His story Oralkk Ethra Mannuvenam , adapted into the film Aaradi , received a Special Jury Mention from the Kerala Film Awards Committee. His novel Tapomayiyude Achan received the Vayalar Award, adding to a body of work that has also been recognised with the Ankanam E. P. Sushama Story Award, Current Books Golden Jubilee Award, V. P. Sivakumar Keli Award, Padmarajan Story Award, and several other literary honours.

b: Haji Syed Salman Chishty is the 26th-generation hereditary key holder of the Sufi Shrine of Dargah Ajmer Sharif and the Gaddi-Nashin of Ajmer Dargah Sharif. His work and public engagement are rooted in Chishty Sufi…
f: Haji Syed Salman Chishty is the 26th-generation hereditary key holder of the Sufi Shrine of Dargah Ajmer Sharif and the Gaddi-Nashin of Ajmer Dargah Sharif. His work and public engagement are rooted in Chishty Sufi thought, Sufi literature and poetry, sacred arts, photography, and interfaith dialogue. A graduate in Economics and Commerce from Wilson College, University of Mumbai, Salman Chishty has devoted his work to exploring how Sufi spiritual traditions, literature and cultural memory can speak to contemporary questions of humanity, peace, pluralism and shared belonging. He has represented the Ajmer Sharif at literary, academic and interfaith forums in India and internationally, including Harvard University, Harvard Divinity School, Johns Hopkins University and the United Nations in New York. His literary and cultural engagements include appearances at the Jaipur Literature Festival, Bradford Literature Festival, Apeejay Kolkata Literature Festival, Kolkata Literature Festival and the Times of India Literature Festival. His discussions have explored themes including Sufi literature and poetry, the legacy of Khwaja Gharib Nawaz, spirituality and modernity, inclusiveness, interfaith dialogue and service to humanity. Salman Chishty is also a founding member, Chairman and Managing Trustee of the Chishty Foundation – Ajmer Sharif, which works across education, humanitarian service and cultural initiatives, while promoting Sufi art, music and the message of Khwaja Gharib Nawaz. His writing includes essays and articles on Islamic spirituality, Sufism, interfaith understanding and Chishty ethics, alongside a continuing body of sacred Sufi photography and reflective “Sufi notes.”

b: Jerry Rao is the founder of Mphasis Corporation, one of India’s leading IT services firms. Before embarking on his entrepreneurial career, he spent over two decades with Citibank and Citicorp, holding senior leadership…
f: Jerry Rao is the founder of Mphasis Corporation, one of India’s leading IT services firms. Before embarking on his entrepreneurial career, he spent over two decades with Citibank and Citicorp, holding senior leadership roles across its global operations. He is also the founder and chairman of Value and Budget Housing Corporation (VBHC), an affordable housing enterprise committed to making quality homes accessible. A leading voice in India’s business and entrepreneurial sphere, Rao has served as the Chairman of NASSCOM and the NASSCOM Foundation. He is also a trustee of the Sujaya Foundation and chairman of the India Foundation for the Arts (IFA). An alumnus of Loyola College, Chennai, IIM Ahmedabad, and the University of Chicago, he has also served as a visiting faculty member at IIM Ahmedabad and IIT Bombay. Beyond business, Rao is closely engaged with the preservation and promotion of India’s history, culture, and the arts. He is also an author whose work spans poetry, essays, history, and political thought, including Gemini II , co-written with C. P. Surendran, as well as Notes from an Indian Conservative , The Indian Conservative , and Economist Gandhi: The Roots and the Relevance of the Political Economy of the Mahatma .

f: Job Kurian is a singer-songwriter and composer known for his distinctive contribution to Malayalam independent music and playback singing. He subsequently established himself as an independent musician and playback singer, known for his expressive vocals, experimental arrangements and storytelling through music. His HOPE Project, comprising the songs “Enthavo”, “Parudeesa”, “Mulla”, and “Kaalam”, explored personal experiences, nostalgia, and social realities through music. He has also been associated with Kappa TV’s Music Mojo and the musical series Straight from the Heart . In Malayalam cinema, Job Kurian has lent his voice to numerous songs, including the hits “Manikya Chirakulla” from Idukki Gold (2013) and “Kaavalaai Chekavar” from Empuraan (2025). Job Kurian won the South Indian International Movie Award (SIIMA) for Best Male Playback Singer in Malayalam in 2023. f: Jobin Joy is a highly accomplished fashion designer with more than twenty years of experience working with leading international and Indian fashion houses. He works in luxury fashion, leading design teams and creating bespoke pieces for celebrities and corporate owners. f: Josy Joseph is a renowned investigative journalist and author, known for his hard-hitting stories on political and corporate corruption in India. He has received prestigious awards, including the Prem Bhatia Award for ‘India’s Best Political Reporter’ (2010) and the Ramnath Goenka Award for ‘Journalist of the Year’ (2013). f: K. E. N. Kunjahammed is a Malayalam writer, cultural critic and public speaker. He retired as the Head of the Department of Malayalam at Farook College, Kozhikode in 2011. He is one of the secretaries of the Progressive Arts and Literature Association (Purogamana Kala Sahithya Sangham) and a member of the Executive Committee of the Kerala Sahitya Akademi. He has written extensively in journals and newspapers, and has authored around thirty books. His writings and public interventions have addressed social and cultural questions including the Kerala renaissance, secularism, caste, communalism, fascism, religion and democracy. His notable works include Swargam, Narakam, Paralokam ( Heaven, Hell, Afterlife) , Samuham, Sahithyam, Samskaram ( Society, Literature, Culture ), Purogama Sahithya Prasthanam: Charithravum Varthamanavum ( The Progressive Literature Movement: History and Present ), Keraleeya Navodhanathinte Charithravum Varthamanavum ( The History and Present of the Kerala Renaissance ), Fascisathinte Adrishya Lokam ( The Invisible World of Fascism ), KEN Sambhashanangal , Iragalude Manifesto , Samskarathile Sangharshangal and Samvadhangalude Album . K. E. N. Kunjahammed has received several literary and cultural honours, including the Kuttippuzha Award, the Gurudarshana Award instituted in the name of Sree Narayana Guru, the Abu Dhabi Sakthi Award and the Thayatt Award. In 2025, he received the Kerala Sahitya Akademi Award for Comprehensive Contribution for 2024.

f: K. K. b: K. P. Ramanunni is a prominent writer in Malayalam literature. He took voluntary retirement from his position as Assistant Manager at the State Bank of India at the age of 42 to focus more on literary and cultural…
f: K. P. Ramanunni is a prominent writer in Malayalam literature. He took voluntary retirement from his position as Assistant Manager at the State Bank of India at the age of 42 to focus more on literary and cultural pursuits. He has served as the editor of Madhyamam weekly and as the administrator of the Thunchan Memorial Trust. He currently serves as adjunct faculty at the Thunchath Ezhuthachan Malayalam University. Ramanunni has received several prestigious awards, including the Kendra Sahitya Akademi Award, Kerala Sahitya Akademi Award, Vayalar Award, Bharatiya Bhasha Parishad Award, and the Asghar Ali Engineer Award. His notable works include Vidhathavinte Chiri , Jaathi Chodhikkuka , Charama Varshikam , Sufi Paranja Katha , Daivathinte Pusthakam , Jeevithathinte Pusthakam , Prakasham Parathunna Aankutti , and Thanthapparatheyyam . His acclaimed novel Sufi Paranja Katha has been translated into English, French, Arabic, Hindi, Bengali, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Konkani, and Maithili. Renowned filmmaker Priyanandanan adapted it into a movie of the same name. His novel Jeevithathinte Pusthakam , set against the backdrop of the lives of people living in a fishing community near Kanhangad, won the Vayalar Award in 2011. The short story Charama Varshikam was published in English as Death Anniversary by Oxford University Press. Ramanunni’s work Daivathinte Pusthakam , which presents a comprehensive depiction of the life of Prophet Muhammad, garnered significant attention. He often represents the Malayalam language at national and international seminars.

Meera uncovered several noteworthy stories, earning her the British Chevening Scholarship for Young Indian Print Journalists, the prestigious PUCL Human Rights Award, the Chowara Parameswaran Award and the Deepalaya National Journalism Award for Child Rights. f: Born in 1946, K. Satchidanandan is a bilingual poet, critic, playwright, editor, fiction writer, and travel writer. He has been a Professor of English and Translation Studies, the editor of the bimonthly “Indian Literature” and “Beyond Borders”, a SAARC literature quarterly, the executive head of the National Academy of Letters, and the National fellow at the Indian Institute of Advanced Study, Shimla. He has won fifty-two literary awards, including the National Academy award, Dante Medal from Italy, Poet Laureate Award from Tata Literature Festival, Mumbai, five awards in five genres from Kerala Sahitya Akademi besides the topmost awards for poetry, and total literary contribution from Kerala, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Maharashtra. He has read his poetry and lectured at several festivals and book fairs in over thirty countries on six continents and translated poetry from across the world. He has also edited dozens of books in Malayalam and English, besides several journals. He has 32 collections of poetry in Malayalam, ten in English, seven in Hindi, and thirty collections in other languages including Arabic, Irish, French, German, Italian, Spanish, Chinese and Japanese, besides all major Indian languages. His latest books of poetry in English include While I Write (HarperCollins), Misplaced Objects and Other Poems (Indian National Academy), The Missing Rib , Not Only the Oceans (Poetrywala, Bombay), The Whispering Tree , No Borders for Me (both Hawakal, Kolkata), I am a Language (Dhauli Books, Bhubaneshwar), Questions from the Dead (Copper Coin, Delhi) and Singing in the Dark (ed. with Nishi Chawla, Penguin-Random House, India). f: K. Suresh Kumar is a retired 1989-batch Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer of the Kerala cadre, widely known for leading the high-profile anti-encroachment drive in Munnar in 2007, during the tenure of former Kerala Chief Minister V. S. Achuthanandan. An engineering graduate from the College of Engineering, Trivandrum (CET), he began his civil service career in 1989 as Revenue Divisional Officer and Sub-Divisional Magistrate in Thiruvalla. In 2007, as the head of a three-member special task force that included IPS officer Rishi Raj Singh and IAS officer Raju Narayana Swamy, he played a central role in demolishing structures identified as illegal encroachments on government land, including properties associated with influential resort owners. Out of his 27 years in the IAS, Suresh Kumar dedicated nearly 16 years to the school education sector in various key capacities, beginning as Deputy Secretary in the General Education Department (1991–1993). He went on to serve as State Project Director of the World Bank-assisted District Primary Education Programme (DPEP), Director of Higher Secondary Education, Director of the State Council of Educational Research and Training (SCERT), Director of Vocational Higher Secondary Education, Joint Secretary to the Government, and Director of the Malayalam Mission. In 1995, the Ministry of Human Resource Development (MHRD), Government of India, nominated him to a two-member country team representing India at a year-long training programme on Modern Educational Practices organized by the Economic Development Institute of the World Bank at its Washington, D.C. headquarters. b: Kalpatta Narayanan is a celebrated novelist, short story writer, essayist, columnist, and poet. Recognized for his significant contributions to Malayalam literature, he has received numerous prestigious awards,…
f: Kalpatta Narayanan is a celebrated novelist, short story writer, essayist, columnist, and poet. Recognized for his significant contributions to Malayalam literature, he has received numerous prestigious awards, including the Basheer Literary Award, Ayyappan Puraskaram, Kerala Sahitya Akademi Award for Literary Criticism, and the Padmaprabha Literary Award. Kalpatta Narayanan is currently the President of the Kerala Sahitya Akademi. Born in a village near Kalpetta, Wayanad in 1952, Kalpatta Narayanan is an esteemed alumnus of the Government Arts and Science College, Kozhikode. His teaching career began as a lecturer at Government Brennen College, Thalassery, followed by a tenure at his alma mater and later as a visiting professor at the University of Calicut. His dynamic speeches at literary and cultural events captivate audiences with their intensity and insight. With a wide readership, Kalpatta Narayanan’s works are celebrated for their depth and appeal. His acclaimed novel Ithra mathram was adapted into a film of the same name in 2012, directed by K. Gopinathan. He has authored numerous poetry collections, critiques, studies, and essays, and contributed columns to various newspapers and periodicals. Among his notable works are Oru Mudanthante Suvishesham , Kavithayude Jeevacharithram , Ethilayum Madhurikkunna Kadukalil , Ee Kannadayonnu Vachu Nokkoo , and Budhapaksham .

b: Karthika V. K. is a publisher at Westland Books. She has spent close to thirty years editing and publishing fiction, non-fiction, translations, poetry, and graphic novels. She began her career at Penguin Books India and…
f: Karthika V. K. is a publisher at Westland Books. She has spent close to thirty years editing and publishing fiction, non-fiction, translations, poetry, and graphic novels. She began her career at Penguin Books India and spent a decade as a publisher at HarperCollins Publishers India, before moving to Westland, where she set up “Context”, an imprint focused on literature and politics. She has published several award-winning and commercially successful writers, including Anita Nair, Aravind Adiga, Manu Joseph, Manu Pillai, Mirza Waheed, Perumal Murugan, M. Mukundan, Rukmini S., and Shashi Deshpande.

b: L. K. Atheeq is a 1991-batch Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer of the Karnataka cadre who retired in January 2025 after 33 years of service. Hailing from Tumakuru, he holds postgraduate degrees in Economics…
f: L. K. Atheeq is a 1991-batch Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer of the Karnataka cadre who retired in January 2025 after 33 years of service. Hailing from Tumakuru, he holds postgraduate degrees in Economics and Agricultural Economics. He has served as Deputy Commissioner of Mandya and Hassan, headed the Karwar Zilla Panchayat, worked on a World Bank-assisted Rural Water Supply and Sanitation Project, and served as State Project Director of Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, the national programme for universal elementary education. At the national and international levels, Atheeq served as Director in the Prime Minister’s Office and represented India on the Board of the World Bank Group in Washington, DC. He served as Principal Secretary to the Karnataka Chief Minister from 2016 to 2018 and subsequently as Additional Chief Secretary to the Chief Minister. During his tenure, he oversaw the state’s finance and treasury management, rural development, and Panchayati Raj portfolios. From 2023 to 2025, Atheeq served as Additional Chief Secretary, Finance Department, and as Additional Chief Secretary to the Chief Minister. He was also a visiting faculty member at the National Law School of India University, Bengaluru, where he taught public finance. He is currently Finance Advisor to the Chief Minister of Karnataka and Chairman of Bengaluru Business Corridor Ltd.

b: M. A. Baby is the General Secretary of the Communist Party of India-Marxist (CPI-M). He took up the post in April 2025 at the party’s 24th Congress in Madurai. He was taking over from Sitaram Yechury and is the second…
f: M. A. Baby is the General Secretary of the Communist Party of India-Marxist (CPI-M). He took up the post in April 2025 at the party’s 24th Congress in Madurai. He was taking over from Sitaram Yechury and is the second Keralite to lead the party, after E. M. S. Namboodiripad. His politics began in school with the Kerala Students Federation, the forerunner of the Students Federation of India. He became the SFI’s Kerala state president in 1975 and went on to become its all-India president in 1979. At 32 he was nominated to the Rajya Sabha, where he served from 1986 to 1998. He later led the Democratic Youth Federation of India. He became a member of the party’s Central Committee in 1989 and the Politburo in 2012. Baby won the Kundara seat in 2006 and 2011 and served the Kerala Government as the Minister for Education and Culture from 2006 to 2011. He is most famous for his work on public education and the close ties he holds with the state’s cultural life. He expresses his opinion on politics, education, and culture through his writings, having authored several notable columns, letters, and statements addressing contemporary Indian politics, Left strategy, and historical analyses. He remains one of the most recognisable voices of the Indian Left.

b: Madhupal Kannambathu is an actor, director, and screenwriter who works in Malayalam cinema. Born on January 1, 1963, in Kozhikode, he made his acting debut with Kashmeeram in 1994 and his directorial debut with…
f: Madhupal Kannambathu is an actor, director, and screenwriter who works in Malayalam cinema. Born on January 1, 1963, in Kozhikode, he made his acting debut with Kashmeeram in 1994 and his directorial debut with Thalappavu (2008), which was about Naxal Varghese, and won several awards in 2008. Kick-starting his film career as an assistant director to eminent filmmakers like Bharath Gopi and Rajiv Anchal, Madhupal has acted in more than 90 films in Malayalam, English, Tamil, and Hindi. He has also contributed to magazines such as Mathrubhumi , Madhyamam , and Bhashaposhini . His recent publications include a short story collection named Irukarakalkidayil Oru Buddhan , published by Mathrubhumi Books in 2024, and Maayaasancharam (2025), a memoir chronicling Madhupal’s journey into cinema. He was the Chairman of the Kerala State Cultural Activist Welfare Fund Board, and is currently a member of both the Kerala State Film Development Corporation (KSFDC) and the Kerala State Chalachithra Academy. Madhupal is the recipient of several awards, such as the Kerala State Television Award for Best Director (2018) for Kaligandaki , the Kerala State Film Award for Second Best Film (2012), the Kerala Film Critics Award for Second Best Film (2012), and the Doordarshan Niravu Best Director Award for Ozhimuri .

b: Manikuttan Paniyan is an Adivasi leader and social worker actively engaged with the tribal communities in Wayanad district. Hailing from the Paniya community, he holds an MBA degree and is dedicated to the social and…
f: Manikuttan Paniyan is an Adivasi leader and social worker actively engaged with the tribal communities in Wayanad district. Hailing from the Paniya community, he holds an MBA degree and is dedicated to the social and economic advancement of Adivasi societies. He is particularly involved in educational initiatives within the Adivasi community. In 2020, he brought attention to the issues faced by Adivasi students who were excluded from Plus One admissions in Wayanad district. Additionally, he was among those who advocated for the inclusion of tribal arts in school youth festivals. Manikuttan Paniyan actively voices his opinions on social issues through his Facebook page. His refusal to contest as the BJP’s candidate in the 2021 Kerala Assembly elections made headlines. “Even if I’m hanged upside down, I will not betray my people,” Manikuttan wrote in a Facebook post accompanied by an image of Ambedkar. He serves as a Teaching Assistant at the Kerala Veterinary and Animal Sciences University. His efforts continue to play a significant role in the upliftment and empowerment of the Adivasi community in Kerala.

b: Manu P. Toms is a journalist with two decades of experience across India’s leading newspapers such as The Hindustan Times and The Hindu Business Line . Having started his career with Malayala Manorama as an editorial…
f: Manu P. Toms is a journalist with two decades of experience across India’s leading newspapers such as The Hindustan Times and The Hindu Business Line . Having started his career with Malayala Manorama as an editorial trainee, Manu shifted to The New Indian Express where he worked as a city reporter. He later became a business reporter. He is currently serving as the Resident Editor of The Economic Times. As a chief of bureau at News Corp and executive editor at ET Prime , he has done investigative stories and led several critical editorial projects. He has led high-performing reporting teams and editorial functions. One of his reports won the Red Ink Award, one of India’s most prestigious journalism awards.

b: Mathew Cherian is a Civil Engineer from BITS Pilani and an alumnus of IRMA, Anand. He started his career in the Corporate Sector and thereafter worked with the National Wasteland Board. He moved by choice to the…
f: Mathew Cherian is a Civil Engineer from BITS Pilani and an alumnus of IRMA, Anand. He started his career in the Corporate Sector and thereafter worked with the National Wasteland Board. He moved by choice to the nonprofit sector heading a number of institutions before retiring after two decades with HelpAge India, serving on the international board as a trustee and Global Ambassador for Ageing. He worked on the national policy for Ageing, served on many Government of India Committees including the grants committee of DST for over a decade, Ministry of Social Justice, High Level Committee on CSR etc. Mathew also initiated the accreditation for the voluntary sector, policy on the nonprofit sector, and serves as Amicus Curiae on the cause of the Elderly in the Supreme Court. Mathew is the recipient of the BITS Pilani Outstanding Alumni Award in 2016, Amir Khusro Award in 2017, Lifetime Achievement Award from ASLI in 2019 and also from Soka Ikeda College for outstanding work in the voluntary sector in 2019. He was Chair of Mobile Creches, Voluntary Action Network India (VANI), Credibility Alliance and Managing trustee of GuideStar India, CARE India and Chair of SAGE for startups in the ageing sector. He is the author of three books: A Million Missions , Managing A Million Missions, and Ageing and Poverty .

b: N. E. Sudheer, born in 1967 in Kannur, Kerala, is a writer and interviewer with decades of experience in literature, politics, and culture. He regularly contributes to Malayalam periodicals, focusing on literary…
f: N. E. Sudheer, born in 1967 in Kannur, Kerala, is a writer and interviewer with decades of experience in literature, politics, and culture. He regularly contributes to Malayalam periodicals, focusing on literary reviews, social issues, and political commentary. Sudheer is known for his secular outlook and, in his own words, “lives without thoughts of caste, religion, or God”. Sudheer’s interviews during literature festivals in Kerala are well-attended and widely appreciated. His interview series Vagvicharam features conversations with figures like Sarah Joseph, Manu S. Pillai, and Sethu, showcasing his skill in extracting nuanced perspectives and fostering meaningful discussions. Sudheer is also the author of Namboodiri Innale , a comprehensive dialogue with the celebrated artist Namboodiri, offering an intimate look into his life and featuring a curated collection of his illustrations. Through his writing and interviews, Sudheer continues to contribute to discussions on culture and society.

b: Narayana Bhattathiri is an artist and pioneer of Malayalam calligraphy, with a career spanning more than four decades. A graduate of the College of Fine Arts, Thiruvananthapuram, he joined the Kalakaumudi group of…
f: Narayana Bhattathiri is an artist and pioneer of Malayalam calligraphy, with a career spanning more than four decades. A graduate of the College of Fine Arts, Thiruvananthapuram, he joined the Kalakaumudi group of publications in 1982 and became the first person in Kerala to be formally designated as a calligrapher. His work has since shaped the visual language of Malayalam lettering across books, magazines, films, and other forms of print culture. Bhattathiri approaches Malayalam letters as a visual and artistic medium, experimenting with their form, movement, and expressive possibilities rather than treating them simply as written language. Over the years, he has designed titles and lettering for numerous Malayalam literary works and films, including works by O. V. Vijayan, M. Mukundan, Malayattoor Ramakrishnan, M. T. Vasudevan Nair, and P. Padmarajan. His work has also been exhibited in India and internationally, including at the Cheongju Cultural Centre in South Korea and the Calligraphy Stone Park in China. A recipient of the Jikji Excellence Award in International Calligraphy, Bhattathiri has played a central role in bringing greater recognition to Malayalam calligraphy. He is the founder of Ka Cha Ta Tha Pa , a gallery dedicated to Malayalam calligraphy in Thiruvananthapuram, and has conducted workshops and classes to encourage a new generation of practitioners. In 2025, he was appointed Honorary Director of the World Calligraphy Association, becoming the first Indian to hold the position. He also serves as Chairman of the Ka Cha Ta Tha Pa Foundation , which promotes calligraphy through exhibitions, workshops, festivals, and educational programmes.

b: Neha Dixit is an independent journalist and author based in New Delhi. She has covered a wide array of topics including politics, gender, and social justice for 20 years, with a particular focus on long-form,…
f: Neha Dixit is an independent journalist and author based in New Delhi. She has covered a wide array of topics including politics, gender, and social justice for 20 years, with a particular focus on long-form, narrative-driven, and investigative pieces. Neha reports for Al Jazeera , The Washington Post , The Caravan , The Wire and other notable publications. Throughout her career, Neha has investigated and exposed numerous human rights violations, including extrajudicial killings by police, hate crimes, human trafficking involving Sangh organizations, clinical trials conducted on marginalized communities by big pharmaceutical companies, and sectarian majoritarian violence in Southasia. In addition to her investigative work, she has also written political profiles and examined the intersections of labor under majoritarian governments. Neha’s journalistic excellence has earned her over a dozen prestigious national and international awards. These include the International Press Freedom Award (2019) from the Committee to Protect Journalists, the Chameli Devi Jain Award for Outstanding Woman Journalist (2017), and the Lorenzo Natali Prize for Journalism (2011) from the European Commission. She has also contributed to several acclaimed non-fiction anthologies. The Many Lives of Syeda X , published by Juggernaut, is her first full-length non-fiction book. It looks at the last 30 years of India through the eyes of a working-class, migrant Muslim woman in Delhi who becomes a part of the cheap female labour economy and takes up over 50 jobs in three decades without once getting paid a minimum wage. Researched for close to a decade, it is a portal to a messy world hidden away from elite Indians. It is the story of untold millions and a searing account of urban life in New India.

b: Nimna Vijay is a Malayalam writer from Kozhikode, known for her works Ettavum Priyappetta Ennodu and Nanayuvan Njan Kadalakunnu . Her debut book, Nanayuvan Njan Kadalakunnu , published in 2021, is a collection of 25…
f: Nimna Vijay is a Malayalam writer from Kozhikode, known for her works Ettavum Priyappetta Ennodu and Nanayuvan Njan Kadalakunnu . Her debut book, Nanayuvan Njan Kadalakunnu , published in 2021, is a collection of 25 stories drawn from people and experiences she encountered at different stages of her life. Nimna’s second book, Ettavum Priyappetta Ennodu , published in May 2023, became a bestseller, with over 1.5 lakh copies sold within a year. The book, which explores the emotional and personal struggles of individuals in contemporary society, reached 34 editions during this period. An English translation of this book is being published by HarperCollins India. She is also a popular social media influencer, with over 100,000 followers on Instagram, and hosts the interview series Pen and Perspective with Nimna Vijay , featuring prominent writers, on her YouTube channel.

b: P. C. Vishnunadh is an Indian National Congress leader and the Minister for Tourism, Culture and Cinema in the Kerala government. He represents the Kundara Assembly constituency in Kollam district. His ministerial…
f: P. C. Vishnunadh is an Indian National Congress leader and the Minister for Tourism, Culture and Cinema in the Kerala government. He represents the Kundara Assembly constituency in Kollam district. His ministerial portfolio includes Tourism, Culture, the Kerala State Film Development Corporation (KSFDC), the Kerala Chalachithra Academy and the Kerala Cultural Activist Welfare Fund Board. Vishnunadh began his political career through the Kerala Students Union (KSU), serving as a student leader at Devaswom Board College, Sasthamcotta. He was elected as the Arts Club Secretary of Devaswom Board College in 1997 and University Union Councillor the next year. Vishnunadh was elected to the Kerala University Senate in 2001 and 2002. He became the state president of KSU in 2002 and subsequently served as president of the Kerala Youth Congress from 2010. He entered the Kerala Legislative Assembly in 2006 after winning the Chengannur constituency, becoming one of the youngest legislators in the state at the time. He retained the seat in 2011. In 2014, he was nominated as the Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) general secretary. In 2017, he was appointed the Secretary of Indian National Congress in charge of Karnataka state. In January 2020, he was appointed the Vice President of Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee. In 2021, Vishnunadh returned to the Assembly by winning the Kundara constituency, defeating then state minister J. Mercykutty Amma. He retained Kundara in the 2026 Kerala Assembly election with 87,862 votes, securing a majority of 32,564 votes. A graduate in commerce from Devaswom Board College, Vishnunadh’s transition from student politics to ministerial office marks a career spanning three decades in Kerala public life.

b: Ahmad, alias P. K. Parakkadavu, hailing from Parakkadavu in Vadakara Taluk, is a renowned short story writer in Malayalam. His style of telling mini-stories or very short tales has a way of winning hearts. With just a…
f: Ahmad, alias P. K. Parakkadavu, hailing from Parakkadavu in Vadakara Taluk, is a renowned short story writer in Malayalam. His style of telling mini-stories or very short tales has a way of winning hearts. With just a few words, he creates powerful scenes that leave a lasting impact, showing his talent for saying a lot with very little. After completing his education at Farook College, he spent many years in the Gulf countries. He was a member of the General Council of the Sahitya Akademi, as well as the Executive Committee of both the Kerala Sahitya Akademi and the Samastha Kerala Sahitya Parishad. He resigned as a protest against the silence of the government and the Akademi following the murders of Kalburgi and other prominent activists. He later served as the Periodicals Editor of the Madhyamam Daily and the Director of Editorial Relations. He was also the Director of the First Madhyamam Literary Fest. He has published 45 books and has also edited one book each on O. V. Vijayan and Vaikom Muhammad Basheer. Mounathinde Nilavili , Thiranjedutha Kathakal , Idiminnalukalude Pranayam and Minnal Kathakal are a few of his famous works. His works have been translated into English, Arabic, and various Indian languages. He is the recipient of the Kerala Sahitya Akademi Award, Kerala Language Institute’s Basheer Memorial Award, SBT Award, Ayanam C. V. Sriraman Award and Abu Dhabi Malayalam Samajam Award.

b: Paranjoy Guha Thakurta is a prominent Indian journalist, author, documentary filmmaker and media educator with over four decades of experience across print and digital media, radio, television and documentary cinema. He…
f: Paranjoy Guha Thakurta is a prominent Indian journalist, author, documentary filmmaker and media educator with over four decades of experience across print and digital media, radio, television and documentary cinema. He began his career in print journalism in 1977, after completing a master’s degree in economics at the University of Delhi. Over the years, he has worked with publications including Business India , Business World , The Telegraph , India Today and The Pioneer . Between 1995 and 2001, he worked with Television Eighteen, anchoring the daily discussion programme India Talks on CNBC-India. From 2007 to 2015, he also anchored weekly programmes on Lok Sabha Television. His work as a documentary filmmaker examines the political economy of contemporary India. His films include Hot as Hell: Why Jharia Is Burning (2006), on the underground coal fires in Jharia, and Coal Curse (2013), which looks into the economy of coal mining in India through the case of Singrauli in Madhya Pradesh. He has directed or co-directed and produced or co-produced more than 25 long-form documentaries and hundreds of podcasts and 16 music videos. Thakurta has authored or co-authored eight books and published more than 30 others, including Gas Wars: Crony Capitalism and the Ambanis (2014), co-authored with Subir Ghosh and Jyotirmoy Chaudhuri, which examines alleged irregularities in natural gas pricing in India. Following the book’s publication, Reliance Industries Limited issued a legal notice to Guha Thakurta and others alleging defamation. In 2016, while serving as editor of Economic and Political Weekly (EPW), he co-authored an article that exposed the government amendments to tax rules that favoured the Adani Group. The group responded with a SLAPP suit, and EPW took the article down.

b: An eminent Malayalam writer, Paul Zacharia is known for his body of literary works comprising short stories, novellas, travelogues, screenplays, essays, columns and writing for children. Zacharia’s notable works include…
f: An eminent Malayalam writer, Paul Zacharia is known for his body of literary works comprising short stories, novellas, travelogues, screenplays, essays, columns and writing for children. Zacharia’s notable works include Oru Nasrani Yuvavum Goulisasthravum , Praise the Lord and Zachariayude Yeshu . He also writes regularly for Kerala’s leading newspapers and magazines, and has been a public speaker for over two decades, often airing non-conformist views on political and religious subjects. A keen traveller, Zacharia has published travelogues on Africa, England, Saudi Arabia and China, and within India, on the Kumbh Mela. In a writing career that spans six decades, he has been the recipient of several awards and honours, such as the Kendra Sahitya Akademi Award, Kerala Sahitya Akademi Award, Ezhuthachan Puraskaram, and more. In November 2013, Zacharia was elected as a Distinguished Fellow of the Kerala Sahitya Akademi. His columns and articles in English have appeared in national periodicals, and his works have been translated into English and several other languages. The Library of Congress has thirteen works by Zacharia in its collection.

b: Pooja Prasanna is the Editorial Head for Reporting at The News Minute , specializing in politics and social justice. With nearly 15 years of experience across broadcast, digital, and print media, she has extensively…
f: Pooja Prasanna is the Editorial Head for Reporting at The News Minute , specializing in politics and social justice. With nearly 15 years of experience across broadcast, digital, and print media, she has extensively covered major news events across South India. Pooja anchors Let Me Explain , a flagship show on The News Minute that offers detailed, unbiased explainers on key news trends from the southern states, providing a 360-degree perspective on significant developments. She also co-hosts and contributes to The South Central Podcast, bringing insightful analysis and in-depth discussions on news and issues from the region. In her role at The News Minute , Pooja manages the reporting section and frequently travels across South India for impactful ground reporting. Before joining The News Minute , she spent several years reporting from South India for national television news networks.

b: Prakash Raj is an established actor, producer, director, television presenter and politician. He is known for his works in South Indian and Hindi films. Starting his acting career in the early 90s, he went on to appear…
f: Prakash Raj is an established actor, producer, director, television presenter and politician. He is known for his works in South Indian and Hindi films. Starting his acting career in the early 90s, he went on to appear in about 400 films. He is the recipient of several accolades, including five National Film Awards, eight Nandi Awards, eight Tamil Nadu State Film Awards, six Filmfare Awards South and many more. A strong critic of the current BJP government, he started his active political movement with the hashtag #justasking on social media after his friend and journalist Gauri Lankesh’s assassination.

b: Prakriti N. V. is a renowned transgender activist and poet. A native of Wayanad, she is the first queer poet from the Adivasi community. She is also the first trans woman from the Paniya community. Her birth name was…
f: Prakriti N. V. is a renowned transgender activist and poet. A native of Wayanad, she is the first queer poet from the Adivasi community. She is also the first trans woman from the Paniya community. Her birth name was Vijeesh, but she later changed it after embracing her identity as a trans woman. Hailing from the Thervayal Adivasi Colony in Naykkatti, Noolpuzha, Wayanad, Prakriti had to overcome numerous challenges in reclaiming her identity.

b: Prashant Bhushan is one of India’s most well-known public interest lawyers in the Supreme Court. He is widely respected for using litigation as a tool for accountability, transparency, and civil liberties. He started…
f: Prashant Bhushan is one of India’s most well-known public interest lawyers in the Supreme Court. He is widely respected for using litigation as a tool for accountability, transparency, and civil liberties. He started his studies at St. Joseph’s College, Allahabad, and later earned a Master’s Degree in Philosophy of Science from Princeton University. He built his reputation taking up cases concerning corruption, the allocation of natural resources, judicial accountability, electoral reform and environmental protection, and has practiced as an Advocate-on-Record before the Supreme Court of India. He is particularly known for the 2G spectrum case and coal allocation scams, both of which drew national attention to questions of transparency in government decision-making. Bhushan has also written extensively on legal and political issues for national newspapers and magazines. His book The Case that Shook India (1978) offers a detailed account of the Indira Gandhi v Raj Narain case, which centred on allegations of electoral malpractice against Prime Minister Indira Gandhi. He has also written Bofors: The Selling of a Nation (1990), which examines the Bofors arms controversy. Bhushan was a central figure in the ‘India Against Corruption’ movement alongside Anna Hazare, and later played a role in the formation of the Aam Aadmi Party before distancing himself from it. He subsequently co-founded the Swaraj Abhiyan, and remains associated with the Sambhaavnaa Institute of Public Policy and Politics, as well as other civil liberties organisations. Bhushan has been a leading supporter of the anti-Modi government protests, from the farmers’ agitation to the CJP protests.

bk.t: Bofors, the selling of a nation

b: Priyanka Gandhi Vadra is a politician and Member of Parliament from Wayanad, Kerala. She is a General Secretary of the Indian National Congress and has been a member of the Lok Sabha since November 2024, when she was…
f: Priyanka Gandhi Vadra is a politician and Member of Parliament from Wayanad, Kerala. She is a General Secretary of the Indian National Congress and has been a member of the Lok Sabha since November 2024, when she was elected from Wayanad. She holds a bachelor’s degree in Psychology from Jesus and Mary College, University of Delhi, and a postgraduate qualification in Buddhist Studies from the University of Sunderland. Priyanka Gandhi has been involved in political and organisational work with the Congress for several decades, initially supporting the election campaigns of her mother, Sonia Gandhi, and brother, Rahul Gandhi. She formally entered electoral politics in 2019, when she was appointed All India Congress Committee (AICC) General Secretary in charge of eastern Uttar Pradesh, and later took responsibility for the state. Her political work has included public outreach and engagement with issues concerning women, farmers, migrant workers, and marginalized communities. Since entering electoral politics, she has become one of the prominent voices against the BJP and its politics of religious polarisation. In Parliament and on the campaign trail, she has criticised the ruling party over issues including farmers’ concerns, the caste census, the handling of Manipur, the treatment of minorities, and the recent SIR deletions.

f: Shuddhabrata Sengupta is an artist, writer and curator, and one of the co-founders of ‘Raqs Media Collective’, established in New Delhi in 1992. Sengupta was the Keith Haring Fellow in Art and Activism at Bard College’s Center for Curatorial Studies and Human Rights Program in 2015–16, and has taught at various academic institutions and independent initiatives. Sengupta is also a co-founder and editor of kafila.org , a platform for critical political commentary and dissent in South Asia. Sukumaran Memorial Literary Award, the Malayattoor Foundation Literary Award, the Akbar Kakkattil Memorial Award, and the Padmarajan Award. He was also selected for the P. Kesavadev Literary Award in 2026 in recognition of his rich contribution to Malayalam literature.

f: Sunny M. Kapikad is a writer and activist from Kottayam. He is an ardent advocate of Dalit rights, vocal about caste discrimination, its manifestation in social and political life, and the marginalisation of the downtrodden. Kapikad’s work was part of a wave of writing in Kerala that reflected the darker side of Indian society, particularly the deprivation and injustice faced by lower caste communities. Kapikad has worked towards publicising Dalit causes, theorising Dalit experiences, and examining their socio-political implications. His notable works include Janathayum Janadhipathyavum: Dalit Vijnanathinte Rashtriya Padangal , Samvaranavum Indian Bharanaghadanayum , among others.

f: T. M. Krishna is an eminent vocalist in the rigorous Karnatik tradition of Indian classical music. Trained under distinguished gurus B. Beyond music, Krishna is a public intellectual who engages with questions of culture, society and the human condition. His books include A Southern Music – The Karnatik Story (2013), a socio-political exploration of Karnatik music that received the Tata Literature Award for Best First Book in Non-Fiction; and Sebastian and Sons (2020), which traces the history of the mrdangam and its makers and received the Tata Literature Live Award for Best Non-Fiction Book. Krishna has also pursued collaborations that bring music into dialogue with social, political and cultural questions. These include the Chennai Poromboke Paadal with environmentalist Nityanand Jayaraman, collaborations with writer Perumal Murugan, and work with the poetry of Sree Narayana Guru. In collaboration with Ashoka University, he is currently involved in “The Edict Project”, which reimagines Emperor Ashoka’s edicts through music. His honours include the Ramon Magsaysay Award (2016), the Indira Gandhi Award for National Integration and Isai Perarignar Award (2017), the Swathi Sangeetha Puraskaram (2019) and the Pasumai Award (2021). In 2025, he was awarded the Sangita Kalanidhi by the Madras Music Academy and the P. Govinda Pillai Nation

b: V. D. Satheesan is the current Chief Minister of Kerala. Born on 31 May 1964 in Nettoor, Kochi, Satheesan received his early education at Panangad High School and completed his pre-degree and Bachelor of Arts in…

f: Yakub Mathew is a global financial leader and transformational thinker with more than three decades in international banking and wealth management. He is currently Managing Director, Investments, at Wells Fargo Advisors, New York, where he has been since 2022. Before that, he spent nearly 12 years at Citi as Managing Director and Head, Asia Business. At HSBC, he served as Senior Vice President and Asian Banking Head in New York (2002-2010), growing the South Asian segment into a significant banking, lending and investment business for HSBC USA. Earlier, he was Head of Expatriate Banking for HSBC in Riyadh. At the start of his career, he set up the Citi NRI business in Manila and Guam, which became a major success story for Citibank Asia Pacific. He holds a BA (Hons) and an MA in Economics from St. Stephen’s College, Delhi, and an MBA from the Asian Institute of Management, Manila. Moving overseas early in his career, he built a path grounded in purpose, professionalism and service. Yakub made his debut as an author with Seeking the Infinite – Maha Kumbh 2025 , which had high-profile launches in New York, Jaipur, New Delhi and Toronto. The multi-faith book on the Mahima of the Kumbh is a powerful reflection on faith, heritage and the universal quest for meaning.
